title: Just a sip of coffee
objective: Assess nutritional needs and choose enteral or parenteral feeding with the dietitian and speech therapist

brief.situation: 08:45 on a medical-surgical unit. Mr. Nakamura, 72, was admitted overnight with a small left-sided stroke and mild right facial droop. His daughter has brought his favorite coffee and asks if he can have it with his morning pills.
handover: Nothing by mouth since admission pending a swallow screen. IV fluid running. His 09:00 oral medicines include his antiplatelet.

Unit stroke policy: a nurse bedside swallow screen before any food, drink or oral medicine; if he fails, nothing by mouth, the provider and the speech-language pathologist told for an evaluation, alternative routes for medicines, and the dietitian for a nutrition plan.
The provider and the speech-language pathologist are on the unit this morning.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and act as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Nakamura failed the swallow screen and his voice is wet. What does it mean, and what do you do?

parts.label: What it means
parts.criteria: Coughing and a wet voice on the screen after a stroke with facial droop is dysphagia with aspiration risk, which can lead to pneumonia; a few weeks of coughing at meals suggests it was already there.
parts.modelAnswer: He has dysphagia from the stroke: he coughed on water and his voice is wet, so liquids and pills could go into his lungs and cause pneumonia.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Nothing by mouth, upright, suction ready; the provider for alternative routes for the medicines; the speech-language pathologist to evaluate; the dietitian for a nutrition plan (enteral if needed); explain to his daughter.
parts.modelAnswer: Keep him upright with nothing by mouth and suction ready, tell the provider so his medicines can go another way, get the speech-language pathologist to assess and the dietitian for a nutrition plan, and explain to his daughter why.

scoring.modelReasoning: After a stroke, nothing goes by mouth, medicines included, until a bedside swallow screen is passed. He sits upright with suction ready. Coughing and a wet voice on the screen are dysphagia with aspiration risk: the provider changes the routes for his medicines, the speech-language pathologist evaluates, and the dietitian plans nutrition, enteral if needed.
